tagline.en: He put Windows on the world's desks, then set out to give the fortune away
tagline.zh: 让 Windows 走上全世界的桌面，再把赚来的钱捐出去

label.en: Pre-IPO Microsoft equity and personal savings (estimate)
label.zh: 微软上市前股权 + 个人储蓄（估算）

label.en: Cascade Investment and other wealth outside Microsoft, net of gifts (estimate)
label.zh: Cascade Investment 等微软以外的财富，已扣除捐赠（估算）

t.en: Seattle Beginnings
t.zh: 西雅图少年

desc.en: A Seattle childhood, a school computer terminal at 13, and two years at Harvard
desc.zh: 在西雅图长大，13 岁在学校机房迷上编程，在哈佛读了两年

t.en: Building Microsoft
t.zh: 创办微软

desc.en: BASIC for the Altair, then the IBM deal that put MS-DOS on almost every PC
desc.zh: 从给 Altair 写 BASIC，到凭 IBM 合约让 MS-DOS 装进几乎每台 PC

t.en: The Windows Empire
t.zh: Windows 帝国

desc.en: IPO, Windows 3.0 and 95, and the title of richest person in the world
desc.zh: 上市、Windows 3.0 与 95，登上世界首富

t.en: Antitrust and Handover
t.zh: 反垄断与交棒

desc.en: The US lawsuit, the $100 billion peak, the CEO handover and the start of the foundation
desc.zh: 美国政府的诉讼、千亿美元的顶点、交出 CEO，基金会起步

t.en: Full-Time Philanthropist
t.zh: 全职慈善家

desc.en: Global health, the Giving Pledge, clean energy, and a shrinking Microsoft stake
desc.zh: 全球健康、捐赠誓言、清洁能源，微软持股不断减少

t.en: Scrutiny and Giving Away
t.zh: 审视与散财

desc.en: Pandemic fame and conspiracy theories, divorce, the 2045 deadline and the Epstein questions
desc.zh: 疫情中的声望与阴谋论、离婚、2045 年期限，以及爱泼斯坦风波

t.en: Born in Seattle, Washington
t.zh: 出生于美国华盛顿州西雅图

summary.en: William Henry Gates III is born in Seattle and grows up there.
summary.zh: 威廉·亨利·盖茨三世出生在西雅图，并在这座城市长大。

why.en: Starting point, not scored. Human capital starts at the average level for a child born in a rich country.
why.zh: 起点事件，不计分；人力资本以发达国家新生儿的平均水平为初始值。

t.en: First hands-on computer time at Lakeside School
t.zh: 在湖滨中学第一次摸到计算机

summary.en: At Lakeside, a private school in Seattle, a teletype terminal linked to a time-sharing computer arrives, paid for by a parents' fundraising sale. Gates, about 13, spends every hour he can on it and teams up with an older student, Paul Allen.
summary.zh: 西雅图私立湖滨中学用家长义卖筹来的钱，装了一台连到分时计算机的电传终端。大约 13 岁的盖茨几乎泡在机房里，并结识了高年级学生保罗·艾伦。

why.en: Rare early access to a computer was the base of everything that followed, so the human-capital target is raised. The story was retold for decades, which adds a small reputation gain.
why.zh: 在那个年代能这么早接触计算机极为罕见，是后来一切的基础，因此上调人力资本目标值；这段经历被反复讲述，口碑系数小幅 +1%。

t.en: Graduates from Lakeside and enrolls at Harvard
t.zh: 湖滨中学毕业，进入哈佛大学

summary.en: Gates finishes Lakeside with the class of 1973 and starts at Harvard College that autumn, where he meets Steve Ballmer.
summary.zh: 盖茨 1973 年从湖滨中学毕业，同年秋天进入哈佛学院，在那里认识了史蒂夫·鲍尔默。

why.en: Education step: the human-capital target rises to about $1 million and the model climbs toward it over roughly a year.
why.zh: 学历台阶：人力资本目标值上调到约 100 万美元，模型用大约一年时间平滑爬升。

t.en: Co-founds Microsoft with Paul Allen in Albuquerque
t.zh: 与保罗·艾伦在阿尔伯克基创立微软

summary.en: After the Altair 8800 kit computer appears, Gates and Allen write a BASIC interpreter for it in about eight weeks and sell it to the maker, MITS. They set up a partnership called Micro-Soft in Albuquerque, New Mexico.
summary.zh: Altair 8800 套件电脑问世后，盖茨和艾伦用约八周时间为它写出 BASIC 解释器，卖给厂商 MITS，并在新墨西哥州阿尔伯克基成立合伙企业 Micro-Soft。

why.en: Life turning point: he now owns part of a company. Financial capital switches from pocket money to founder equity, valued here from the company's early sales. The figures are estimates.
why.zh: 人生转折点：开始持有一家公司的股权。金融资本从零花钱切换为创始人股权，按公司早期营收粗略估值，数字为估算。

fin.en: Founder equity enters the model (interpolated between rough private estimates)
fin.zh: 创始人股权进入模型（私有期按粗略估值插值）

t.en: Takes leave from Harvard and never returns
t.zh: 从哈佛休学，此后再未回校

summary.en: Gates takes a leave of absence from Harvard to work full time on the software business. He does not go back to finish his degree.
summary.zh: 盖茨向哈佛申请休学，全职投入软件生意，此后没有回去完成学位。

why.en: Mixed at the time: he gives up a degree but gains years of head start. The dropout story later becomes part of his public image, so reputation gets a small lift.
why.zh: 当时看利弊参半：放弃了学位，换来几年先发优势。“辍学创业”后来成为他公众形象的一部分，口碑系数小幅 +1%。

t.en: Signs the deal to supply the IBM PC's operating system
t.zh: 签下为 IBM PC 提供操作系统的合约

summary.en: IBM approaches Microsoft in July 1980 and the papers are signed in early November. Microsoft licenses, then buys, a system called 86-DOS from Seattle Computer Products and adapts it as PC DOS. The IBM PC ships with it on August 12, 1981, and Microsoft stays free to sell its own version, MS-DOS, to other computer makers.
summary.zh: IBM 于 1980 年 7 月找到微软，11 月初签约。微软先从西雅图计算机产品公司取得 86-DOS 的授权，随后将其买下，改造成 PC DOS。1981 年 8 月 12 日 IBM PC 搭载它上市，而微软保留了把自家版本 MS-DOS 卖给其他电脑厂商的权利。

why.en: The most valuable contract of his career: the right to license the system to every PC clone maker. The private valuation steps up sharply over the following years, and reputation gains 3%.
why.zh: 职业生涯中最值钱的一纸合约：可以把系统授权给所有兼容机厂商。此后几年私有估值大幅抬升，口碑系数 +3%。

fin.en: Private stake estimate: about $10 million in 1980 to about $100 million in 1983
fin.zh: 私有持股估值：1980 年约 1,000 万美元 → 1983 年约 1 亿美元

t.en: Microsoft goes public on Nasdaq at $21 a share
t.zh: 微软在纳斯达克上市，发行价 21 美元

summary.en: Microsoft raises $61 million in its initial public offering. The shares open at $21 and close the first day at $28. Gates keeps about 45% of the company.
summary.zh: 微软首次公开募股筹资 6,100 万美元，发行价 21 美元，首日收于 28 美元。盖茨保留约 45% 的股份。

why.en: Anchor switch: from this day financial capital = ownership × shares outstanding × the daily MSFT close (split-adjusted; Microsoft has split nine times, a combined factor of 288).
why.zh: 锚点切换：从这一天起，金融资本 = 持股比例 × 总股本 × MSFT 当日收盘价（拆股复权；微软先后拆股九次，累计 288 倍）。

fin.en: About 45% of Microsoft, worth roughly $235 million at the offer price; priced daily from MSFT afterwards
fin.zh: 约 45% 的微软股份，按发行价约值 2.35 亿美元；此后按 MSFT 日线逐日计价

t.en: Forbes lists him as a billionaire at age 31
t.zh: 31 岁登上《福布斯》十亿美元富豪榜

summary.en: A year after the IPO, Forbes puts his fortune at $1.25 billion, making him the youngest self-made billionaire up to that time.
summary.zh: 上市一年后，《福布斯》估算他的身家为 12.5 亿美元，他成为当时最年轻的白手起家十亿美元富豪。

why.en: The money itself is already in the stock price. The "youngest billionaire" label adds 2% to reputation.
why.zh: 财富本身已由股价体现；“最年轻十亿富豪”的标签让口碑系数 +2%。

t.en: Windows 3.0 launches and finally catches on
t.zh: Windows 3.0 发布，Windows 终于流行起来

summary.en: Windows 1.0 had shipped on November 20, 1985 to a lukewarm reception. Version 3.0 is the first to sell in large numbers and makes a graphical desktop the norm on IBM-compatible PCs.
summary.zh: 1985 年 11 月 20 日发布的 Windows 1.0 反响平平。3.0 版第一次大卖，让图形界面成为 IBM 兼容机的标配。

why.en: Sales show up in the stock price. Defining the standard PC desktop is a lasting reputation asset, so reputation gains 2%.
why.zh: 销量由股价反映；定义了 PC 桌面的标准，是长期声誉资产，口碑系数 +2%。

t.en: Tops the Forbes 400 for the first time
t.zh: 首次登顶《福布斯》美国 400 富豪榜

summary.en: Forbes names Gates, then 36, the richest person in the United States with an estimated $6.3 billion, nearly all of it Microsoft stock.
summary.zh: 《福布斯》把 36 岁的盖茨列为美国首富，估算身家 63 亿美元，几乎全部是微软股票。

why.en: Wealth is carried by the MSFT price. The ranking itself lifts his media baseline and adds 2% to reputation.
why.zh: 财富由 MSFT 股价体现；榜单本身抬高了媒体热度基线，口碑系数 +2%。

src.name: The Harvard Crimson · Gates named richest in U.S. (1992-10-06)

t.en: Forbes ranks him the world's richest person
t.zh: 被《福布斯》列为世界首富

summary.en: Forbes puts his fortune at $12.9 billion on its 1995 list and ranks him first among individuals worldwide. He holds or shares the top spot in most years through 2017.
summary.zh: 《福布斯》1995 年榜单估算他的身家为 129 亿美元，在全球个人富豪中排名第一。此后直到 2017 年，他在多数年份占据榜首。

why.en: Wealth is carried by the MSFT price. "The richest person in the world" becomes his global label: reputation +2% and a much higher media baseline. Around now the model also starts a second holding for wealth outside Microsoft (Cascade Investment). Tallies differ on the first year at number one; some lists start it in 1997.
why.zh: 财富由 MSFT 股价体现；“世界首富”成为他的全球标签，口碑系数 +2%，媒体热度基线大幅抬升。模型也从这一时期开始单列微软之外的财富（Cascade Investment）。各榜单对他首次登顶的年份说法不一，有的从 1997 年算起。

fin.en: Second holding begins: diversified wealth outside Microsoft, an estimate
fin.zh: 第二项持仓起算：微软之外的多元化财富（估算）

t.en: Writes "The Internet Tidal Wave" memo
t.zh: 写下《互联网浪潮》备忘录

summary.en: In a memo to his executives, Gates calls the internet the most important development since the IBM PC and orders every product group to put it first. Microsoft bundles its Internet Explorer browser with Windows soon after.
summary.zh: 盖茨在给高管的备忘录里称，互联网是 IBM PC 之后最重要的变化，要求所有产品部门把它放在第一位。不久后微软把 IE 浏览器与 Windows 捆绑。

why.en: A fast strategic turn by a dominant company. The stock carries the business result; reputation gains 2% for the call. The same memo was later used as evidence in the antitrust trial.
why.zh: 行业霸主的一次快速转向。业务结果由股价体现，这次判断让口碑系数 +2%。这份备忘录后来也成了反垄断案的证据。

src.name: US Department of Justice · Trial exhibit: "The Internet Tidal Wave" memo

t.en: Windows 95 launches as a worldwide event
t.zh: Windows 95 发布，成为全球事件

summary.en: Windows 95 goes on sale with a huge marketing campaign and sells more than a million copies in its first four days.
summary.zh: Windows 95 在声势浩大的营销中上市，头四天就卖出一百多万份。

why.en: Sales are in the stock price. The launch makes Gates a household name well beyond the industry: reputation +3% and a jump in audience.
why.zh: 销量由股价反映；这次发布让盖茨的名字走出行业、家喻户晓，口碑系数 +3%，受众规模跃升。

t.en: US government and 20 states sue Microsoft
t.zh: 美国司法部与 20 个州起诉微软

summary.en: The Justice Department, 20 states and the District of Columbia sue Microsoft, saying it used its Windows monopoly to crush rival browsers. The case shapes the next three years of Gates's working life.
summary.zh: 美国司法部联合 20 个州和哥伦比亚特区起诉微软，指其利用 Windows 的垄断地位打压竞争对手的浏览器。此后三年，这场官司主导了盖茨的工作。

why.en: The legal risk is priced by the market. The damage to his personal image, from admired founder to accused monopolist, is not in the price, so reputation takes a 4% hit.
why.zh: 法律风险由市场定价；但他个人形象从受人敬仰的创始人变成被控垄断者，这部分股价看不到，口碑系数 -4%。

src.name: US Department of Justice · Complaint, U.S. v. Microsoft
Wikipedia · United States v. Microsoft Corp.

t.en: Videotaped deposition in the antitrust case
t.zh: 在反垄断案中接受录像取证

summary.en: Gates gives a videotaped deposition. Clips played in court show him disputing the meaning of ordinary words and often saying he does not recall. Press accounts describe him as evasive.
summary.zh: 盖茨接受录像取证。法庭上播放的片段里，他对一些普通词语的含义反复争辩，多次表示“不记得”，媒体形容他回避问题。

why.en: A pure reputation event that the share price did not register: reputation -3%.
why.zh: 纯声誉事件，股价没有反应：口碑系数 -3%。

src.name: Wikipedia · United States v. Microsoft Corp.

t.en: Net worth briefly passes $100 billion
t.zh: 身家一度突破 1,000 亿美元

summary.en: At the height of the dot-com boom his fortune briefly passes $100 billion, the first time any person is reported to reach that level. In the same year he gives Microsoft shares worth about $16 billion to his foundation.
summary.zh: 互联网泡沫最盛之时，他的身家一度突破 1,000 亿美元，是有报道以来第一个达到这一水平的人。同年他把价值约 160 亿美元的微软股票捐给了自己的基金会。

why.en: Entirely a share-price effect, so no reputation points. His ownership falls from about 21% to about 15% in the model as shares move to the foundation. Ownership figures are estimates from public filings.
why.zh: 完全是股价效应，不加口碑分。随着股票转入基金会，模型中的持股比例从约 21% 降到约 15%。持股比例为根据公开披露所做的估算。

fin.en: MSFT stake about $90 billion at the December 1999 peak, plus about $10 billion elsewhere
fin.zh: 1999 年 12 月高点时微软持股约 900 亿美元，另有约 100 亿美元其他资产

src.name: Fortune · Gates's $4.6 billion donation, largest since 2000

t.en: The Bill & Melinda Gates Foundation takes shape
t.zh: 比尔及梅琳达·盖茨基金会成形

summary.en: The family's earlier charities, begun in 1994, are merged into one foundation focused on global health, development and US education. With the share gifts of 1999 and 2000 it becomes one of the largest private foundations in the world.
summary.zh: 家族自 1994 年起设立的慈善机构合并为一家基金会，聚焦全球健康、发展和美国教育。加上 1999、2000 年捐入的股票，它成为全球最大的私人基金会之一。

why.en: Gifts lower financial capital, and the model shows that through falling ownership. What the price cannot see is the start of a second career in philanthropy: reputation +5%, released slowly.
why.zh: 捐赠会减少金融资本，模型通过持股比例下降来体现。股价看不到的是他慈善“第二职业”的开端：口碑系数 +5%，缓慢释放。

t.en: Hands the CEO job to Steve Ballmer
t.zh: 把 CEO 一职交给史蒂夫·鲍尔默

summary.en: After 25 years in charge, Gates makes Ballmer chief executive. He stays on as chairman and takes a new title, chief software architect.
summary.zh: 执掌公司 25 年后，盖茨让鲍尔默出任首席执行官，自己留任董事长，并担任新设的“首席软件架构师”。

why.en: A planned handover in the middle of the antitrust fight. Markets priced it; no reputation change. The human-capital target is trimmed because he is no longer the operating chief.
why.zh: 反垄断案期间的一次有计划交接。市场已定价，口碑系数不变；由于不再担任一把手，人力资本目标值略降。

src.name: HistoryLink · Gates hands Microsoft leadership to Ballmer
CBS News · Gates gives up Microsoft helm

t.en: Judge orders Microsoft split in two
t.zh: 法官下令将微软一分为二

summary.en: Judge Thomas Penfield Jackson had found on November 5, 1999 that Microsoft held a monopoly, and on April 3, 2000 that it broke antitrust law. He now orders the company divided into an operating-system business and an applications business.
summary.zh: 托马斯·彭菲尔德·杰克逊法官先在 1999 年 11 月 5 日认定微软拥有垄断地位，又在 2000 年 4 月 3 日裁定其违反反垄断法，此时下令把公司拆成操作系统和应用软件两家企业。

why.en: The share price had already fallen hard that spring and carries the financial side. Reputation loses another 2% for the low point of the case.
why.zh: 股价在当年春天已大幅下跌，金融影响由股价体现；案件走到最低谷，口碑系数再 -2%。

src.name: US Department of Justice · Court's Findings of Fact
Wikipedia · United States v. Microsoft Corp.

t.en: Appeals court throws out the breakup order
t.zh: 上诉法院推翻拆分令

summary.en: A federal appeals court reverses the order to split Microsoft, while upholding the finding that it illegally maintained a monopoly. The Justice Department drops its demand for a breakup in September and settles with the company in November 2001.
summary.zh: 联邦上诉法院推翻了拆分微软的命令，但维持其非法维持垄断的认定。司法部 9 月放弃拆分要求，并于 2001 年 11 月与微软达成和解。

why.en: The company survives intact, which the stock reflects. Reputation recovers by 1%; the monopoly finding stands.
why.zh: 公司得以保全，由股价反映；口碑系数回升 1%，但垄断认定依然成立。

src.name: Wikipedia · United States v. Microsoft Corp.

t.en: Warren Buffett pledges most of his fortune to the foundation
t.zh: 沃伦·巴菲特承诺把大部分财富捐给基金会

summary.en: Buffett promises about 10 million Berkshire Hathaway class B shares to the Gates Foundation, paid in yearly installments. The same month Gates says he will move to full-time foundation work within two years.
summary.zh: 巴菲特承诺向盖茨基金会捐出约 1,000 万股伯克希尔·哈撒韦 B 类股，按年分批交付。同月，盖茨宣布将在两年内转为全职从事基金会工作。

why.en: The gift is Buffett's money, not Gates's, so financial capital is unchanged. The world's second-richest person trusting him with his fortune is a strong endorsement: reputation +3%.
why.zh: 这笔捐赠是巴菲特的钱，不是盖茨的，金融资本不变。世界第二富豪把财富托付给他，是极强的背书：口碑系数 +3%。

src.name: Microsoft · Plans for July 2008 transition for Bill Gates (2006-06-15)

t.en: Last full-time day at Microsoft
t.zh: 在微软的最后一个全职工作日

summary.en: Following the two-year plan announced in 2006, Gates ends his day-to-day role at Microsoft to work full time at the foundation. He remains chairman of the board.
summary.zh: 按照 2006 年公布的两年过渡计划，盖茨结束在微软的日常工作，全职投入基金会，同时继续担任董事长。

why.en: A career change by choice. Future earning power from running a company falls, so the human-capital target is lowered; the move into full-time giving adds 2% to reputation.
why.zh: 主动选择的职业转换。经营企业带来的未来收入能力下降，人力资本目标值下调；全职做慈善让口碑系数 +2%。

src.name: Microsoft · Plans for July 2008 transition for Bill Gates (2006-06-15)

t.en: Launches the Giving Pledge with Warren Buffett
t.zh: 与巴菲特共同发起“捐赠誓言”

summary.en: Gates, Melinda French Gates and Buffett ask the world's richest people to commit at least half of their wealth to charity. By August 2010, 40 people have signed.
summary.zh: 盖茨、梅琳达·弗伦奇·盖茨和巴菲特呼吁全球最富有的人承诺捐出至少一半财富。到 2010 年 8 月，已有 40 人签署。

why.en: No money changes hands, so this is reputation only: +3%. The pledge is a public promise, not a legal contract.
why.zh: 没有资金易手，只影响声誉：口碑系数 +3%。誓言是公开承诺，不具法律约束力。

t.en: Gives up the chairman's seat as Satya Nadella becomes CEO
t.zh: 纳德拉出任 CEO，盖茨卸任董事长

summary.en: Microsoft names Satya Nadella chief executive. Gates leaves the chairman's role, stays on the board and becomes technology adviser to the new CEO.
summary.zh: 微软任命萨提亚·纳德拉为首席执行官。盖茨卸任董事长，留任董事，并出任新 CEO 的技术顾问。

why.en: His MSFT stake is about 4% by now, so the stock's long rise under Nadella helps him less than it once would have. Small reputation gain for a smooth succession.
why.zh: 此时他持有的微软股份约为 4%，纳德拉时代股价的长期上涨对他的拉动已不如从前。交接平稳，口碑系数小幅 +1%。

src.name: Microsoft · Board names Satya Nadella as CEO (2014-02-04)

t.en: Launches the Breakthrough Energy Coalition at the Paris climate talks
t.zh: 在巴黎气候大会上发起“突破能源联盟”

why.en: Financial capital falls by the size of the gift; the model shows it as ownership sliding from about 2.5% to 1.3%. A small reputation gain.
why.zh: 金融资本按捐赠规模减少，模型体现为持股比例从约 2.5% 降到 1.3%；口碑系数小幅 +1%。

why.zh: 这是对未来捐赠的承诺，当天金融资本不变，今后每笔捐出时再相应下调。它给整个事业定下了终点日期：口碑系数 +5%。
